metadata.title: The Missing Heir
metadata.description: Investigate the disappearance of a wealthy businessman's son who vanished under mysterious circumstances.
metadata.briefing: Thomas Blackwood Jr., son of CEO Thomas Blackwood Sr., disappeared after leaving his apartment at 2:30 PM on December 15. The family's prominence demands urgency and discretion.

assets.description: Official case assignment document from Chief of Police with preliminary details.

assets.title: Photo of Thomas Blackwood Jr.
assets.description: Recent photograph of the missing person taken at a company event three weeks ago.

assets.title: Victim's Mobile Phone
assets.description: Thomas Jr.'s smartphone found in his apartment, locked but intact. Likely holds call logs, messages and app data.

assets.description: Detailed report from the digital forensics lab summarizing the recovered call history, deleted messages and GPS data.

emails.subject: URGENT: Missing Person Case Assignment
emails.body:
Detective Morgan,

You've been assigned to investigate the disappearance of Thomas Blackwood Jr., a 28-year-old software engineer who went missing yesterday afternoon. He was last seen leaving his downtown Portland apartment at 2:30 PM.

His father, Thomas Blackwood Sr., CEO of Blackwood Industries, reported him missing this morning when Thomas Jr. failed to attend a critical board meeting. Given the Blackwood family's prominence, handle this with urgency and discretion.

The initial briefing and a recent photo of Thomas Jr. are attached.

Chief Mitchell
Portland Police Department

emails.subject: Digital Forensics Analysis — Phone Dump
emails.body:
Detective Morgan,

Digital forensics on the iPhone 14 Pro recovered from Thomas Blackwood Jr.'s apartment is complete.

Key findings:

1. **Last activity:** device used at 2:15 PM on December 15th, about 15 minutes before he was last seen.
2. **Call logs:** three outgoing calls on the day of disappearance — to his father (10:30 AM, 4 min), to an unknown number 503-555-0142 (1:45 PM, 12 min) and to the same number (2:10 PM, 2 min). The unknown number traces back to a burner phone purchased at a convenience store in Northeast Portland.
3. **Text messages:** deleted messages recovered from the unknown-number conversation suggest a planned meeting at an undisclosed location.
4. **Location data:** GPS history shows the victim visited 1247 Riverside Drive twice in the week before disappearance. Property is registered to Marcus Reeve.

Full report attached.

Tech Specialist Rodriguez
Digital Forensics Lab

suspects.name: Thomas Blackwood Sr.
suspects.motive: Recent financial disputes with son over company succession and ethics disagreements.
suspects.alibi: Claims to have been at company board meeting from 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM on December 15th.
suspects.background: Thomas Blackwood Sr. is a self-made multi-millionaire who built Blackwood Industries over 30 years. Demanding and controlling, recently in conflict with Thomas Jr. over ethically questionable deals.

suspects.name: Marcus Reeve
suspects.motive: Possible blackmail — internal company memos suggest Reeve was paid for fixer work and recently demanded more.
suspects.alibi: No verified alibi for the afternoon of December 15th.
suspects.background: Owner of the property at 1247 Riverside Drive visited by the victim twice in the prior week. Burner phone linked to him in forensic phone dump.

suspects.name: Eva Blackwood
suspects.motive: Stood to gain Thomas Jr.'s board seat and the succession line.
suspects.alibi: Says she was on a conference call with the European division from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM.
suspects.background: Has clashed with Thomas Jr. publicly over executive bonuses but the conference call was independently verified by the European team.

timeline.event: Thomas Jr. takes 12-min call from burner phone (503-555-0142).
Thomas Jr. last seen leaving his apartment building.
Thomas Blackwood Sr. reports his son missing after failed board meeting.

payload.message: The Chief expects an initial status update within the hour. Prioritize the phone forensics.

actions.message: GPS history places the victim at Marcus Reeve's address twice. Worth a closer look.

rules.description: Eva's alibi was independently verified before the case opened — surface that the moment the detective reads the briefing.

forensicOutcomes.conclusionText: Burner phone calls + GPS history place the victim at Marcus Reeve's property twice in the week before disappearance.
No usable prints recovered from the photographic print surface.

solution.explanation: The phone forensics tied a burner number to Marcus Reeve, whose property the victim visited twice in the prior week. Eva's alibi was independently verified by the European team. Thomas Sr. was at a board meeting attended by multiple witnesses.
